newsitem.title: POLAND: BIG-Gdanski merger to cut costs.
newsitem.headline: BIG-Gdanski merger to cut costs.

text.p: The merger between Poland's Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych SA (BIG) and Bank Gdanski SA will save between 80 million and 100 million zlotys per year starting from 1999, BIG's president said on Wednesday.
"We expect to save 80 to 100 million zlotys per year from 1999," Boguslaw Kott told a news conference.
"It will be most effective to merge the two banks into one banking organism...which would allow for a considerable synergy of costs, asset allocation and for better sales," he said.
Kott said that after the merger the new banking entity, expected to be called BIG Bank GDANSKI SA, would concentrate on retail sector clients and small companies.
"The most important sector...will be retail...and also offers to small and mid-sized firms," he said.
BIG Bank GDANSKI would be the seventh largest Polish bank ranked according to total assets, amounting to 7.9 billion zlotys, and fifth in terms of own funds, at 866 million zlotys. @

Shareholders of Gdanski and BIG are expected to decide on their merger in late June. To conclude the merger, planned to take effect by the end of September, an exchange of 11 BIG shares for one Gdanski share will take place.
